newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa, UAP complete in 3 to 4 years.
newsitem.headline: Axa, UAP complete in 3 to 4 years.

text.p: The reorganisation of French insurers Axa and Unions des Assurances de Paris (UAP) will take three or four years and will probably involve some job reduction through attrition, a source close to UAP said on Monday.
The source said the merger would probably also involve putting some full time workers on a part time footing.
Axa and UAP said last week said they planned to merge to forge the world's second-largest insurance company.
"The reorganisation will happen over three or four years," the source said, adding that this period would allow the progressive management of any overstaffing.
Axa has 8,000 employees and 3,200 independent agents in France and UAP has 18,000 staff and 1,500 independent agents.

"With the independent agents, there is a cultural and traditional difference, but there will be a group consultation on the change," the source said. "If we do it right, we can do it without tragedy on the employment front."
The source said the progressive change could involve attrition and the use of part time work.
At the announcement of their merger plan, the two companies said there would be no mass layoffs in France.
The merger will produce synergies in Europe but will also result in overlap in France, Belgium and Britain, experts said.
